Leg 2 · On the ground

Five nights in Iceland — the day plans

Monday, Dec 14 to Saturday, Dec 19, based in Reykjavík the whole time. Mid-December daylight is roughly 11:15 AM to 3:45 PM, about 4½ hours — so every plan below does the same trick the TikTok itineraries do: drive in the dark, put the big sights inside the daylight window, and use the long night for lagoons, food, and the northern lights.

At a glance

Four tour days, one gentle arrival day, and a northern-lights attempt most nights — because one clear night is luck, three or four attempts is a strategy. If winter weather cancels a day, swap it with Friday: Friday is deliberately the flex day until you lock the ice cave.

How this was planned: built from the Iceland itineraries that get saved over and over on TikTok — the 6-day winter route from @lance.drives, plus @allthingsiceland and @adventures.is — then re-timed for a Reykjavík base and 4½ hours of daylight instead of a moving road trip. The TikTok consensus, applied on every day below:
1 · Don't self-drive the big daysGolden Circle, South Coast, Snæfellsnes, and the glacier lagoon are all bookable as guided day tours from Reykjavík. In December that means no icy-road driving, no headlight stress, and a driver watching road.is so you don't have to.
2 · Check two sites every morningroad.is for closures and vedur.is for wind + the aurora cloud map. A red road means closed, not "drive carefully" — that's the day you swap to the city plan.
3 · Book the winter-only things firstNatural blue ice caves only run roughly November–March, and northern-lights tours usually let you rejoin free if the lights don't show. Book both early, chase the aurora from night one.
Mon · Dec 14 · Arrival day

Reykjavík, gently — beat jet lag, don't fight it

You land at 10:00 AM feeling like it's 5:00 AM. TikTok arrival days that work all do the same thing: daylight walk, viral snack, hot water at dusk, early night. No tour today.

On foot onlyDaylight window ~12:30–3:45 PMNight 1: aurora only if you're awake
  • 12:30 PMCheck in, unpack, short reset. 20–30 min nap max if you need it — a long sleep now wrecks tomorrow's 8:30 AM start.
  • 1:00 PMBrauð & Co — the cinnamon roll (snúður).TikTok viral The graffiti-covered bakery near Hallgrímskirkja is in half the Reykjavík food videos on the app for a reason. Warm roll + coffee is the jet-lag cure.
  • 1:30–3:30 PMThe daylight walk: up Skólavörðustígur (Rainbow Street) to Hallgrímskirkja — take the tower lift for the city view while it's light — then down to the Old Harbour, Harpa concert hall (free to walk inside, glass facade glows at dusk), and the Sun Voyager sculpture on the waterfront for golden-hour photos.
  • 3:45 PMBæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the famous hot dog stand.TikTok viral Order like a local: einn með öllu — one with everything (crispy + raw onion, ketchup, sweet mustard, remoulade). It's dark already; that's normal, embrace it.
  • 5:00–7:00 PMSky Lagoon at dusk. 15 min from downtown, infinity edge over the Atlantic, and the 7-step ritual (lagoon → cold plunge → sauna → cold mist → steam → scrub → lagoon). TikTok's pick over Blue Lagoon for a city base: same geothermal soak, no 45-min drive, and sunset-into-dark from 38–40°C water is a December-only version of it. Book the ~4:30–5:00 PM slot ahead.
  • EveningChristmas lights + early bed. Ingólfstorg square has the ice rink and market stalls in December, and a Yule Lad arrives each night from Dec 12. Dinner near Laugavegur, bed by ~10 PM. Check vedur.is — if it's unexpectedly clear, Grótta lighthouse (10 min) is the in-city aurora spot.
Why Sky Lagoon today, not Blue Lagoon: Blue Lagoon is back out by the airport. Save it as an either/or for Friday's flex plan — doing both lagoons in 5 days is the classic first-timer overspend.
Tue · Dec 15 · Tour day 1

Golden Circle — the one everyone saves first

The ~250 km loop in almost every Iceland TikTok: walk between two tectonic plates, watch a geyser erupt, stand over a half-frozen waterfall — and in winter it fits almost exactly inside the daylight you get.

Guided tour or self-driveDepart ~8:30 AM · back ~6:30 PMSights in daylight ~11 AM–3:45 PM
  • 8:30 AMLeave Reykjavík in the dark. That's the plan, not a problem — the drive out is the twilight part. Coffee and a Brauð & Co pastry for the road.
  • ~10:45 AMÞingvellir National Park as it gets light. Walk the Almannagjá gorge in the rift between the North American and Eurasian plates, out to the Öxarárfoss waterfall. Paths can be icy — this is the day for crampons / ice cleats if you packed them.
  • 12:15 PMGeysir geothermal area. Strokkur erupts every few minutes, up to ~30 m — film it twice, it rarely fires the same way twice. Lunch across the road, or push lunch to Friðheimar (below).
  • 1:30 PMGullfoss in the best light of the day. The two-tier falls, often part-frozen in December with icicle curtains. Upper viewpoint if the lower path is closed for ice (it often is Nov–Mar). Waterproof jacket — the spray is real.
  • AfternoonThe TikTok add-ons, pick by time: Friðheimar tomato farm — soup and fresh bread inside a working greenhouse, the most-shared Golden Circle lunch on TikTok; and/or Kerið crater — red slopes around a frozen lake, short stop, very photogenic in snow.
  • Drive backDark drive home = free aurora watch. Golden Circle countryside is dark enough that tours stop if the lights appear on the return. Keep looking out the window.
  • 9:00 PMNorthern Lights tour — Night 1 attempt (book this one). Small-group bus tour out of the city, ~3–4 hrs. Book it for tonight, not Friday: if it's cloudy or the lights don't show, most operators let you rejoin another night free, so starting early buys you retries Tue–Fri.
Swap rule: if road.is shows the Golden Circle loop closed for a storm, swap today with Friday's city flex plan and run the Circle on the next clear day. It is the easiest drive of the four, so it is also the best bad-weather backup.
Wed · Dec 16 · Tour day 2

South Coast to Vík — waterfalls + the black beach

The most-saved day in the TikTok winter routes: two huge waterfalls, a hidden one in a cave, and the black-sand beach — sequenced east so the beach lands in the last, best light.

Guided tour strongly recommendedDepart ~8:00 AM · back ~7:30 PMWaterfalls from ~10:30 AM
  • 8:00 AMDepart in the dark, east on Route 1. This is a long day — waterproof pants and boots today, you will get sprayed.
  • ~10:30 AMSeljalandsfoss. The falls you can normally walk behind — in December that path is usually closed for ice, so the move is the front view plus the short walk to Gljúfrabúi, the hidden falls tucked in a small canyon right next to it.
  • ~11:45 AMSkógafoss + Kvernufoss. Skógafoss is the big, loud one you can walk right up to. Kvernufoss, a 10-min walk from the Skógar museum car park, is the TikTok one: a falls inside a half-cave that most tour buses skip.
  • ~1:15 PMSólheimajökull glacier viewpoint (short walk to the ice edge on a guided stop) and lunch in Vík — the little town with the church on the hill and the black-beach view from above.
  • ~2:30 PMReynisfjara black sand beach in the last light.TikTok famous Basalt columns, sea stacks offshore, black sand with snow on it. This is the photo — and the one place on the trip where the warning matters more than the photo (see below).
  • EveningDark drive back to Reykjavík, dinner in town. Aurora attempt #3 happens on the drive and, if it's clear, again from Grótta — no separate tour needed tonight unless Tuesday's rejoin is still unused.
Reynisfjara safety — non-negotiable: sneaker waves here are dangerous and unpredictable, worst in winter. Stay well back from the waterline, never turn your back on the ocean, and obey the warning-light system at the entrance — no photo is worth ignoring it.
Thu · Dec 17 · Tour day 3

Snæfellsnes — "Iceland in miniature" + Kirkjufell

One peninsula with a bit of everything — lava fields, cliffs, a black church, a glacier volcano — ending at Kirkjufell, the mountain in this page's header photo and one of the most-filmed spots in the country.

Guided day tourDepart ~8:00 AM · back ~8:00 PMKirkjufell in afternoon light
  • MorningDrive north-west in the dark, through the Hvalfjörður tunnel. First light hits as you reach the peninsula's south coast.
  • ~11:00 AMBúðir black church + Arnarstapi cliffs. The lone black church in a lava field is a 30-second TikTok staple; Arnarstapi is the cliff walk — sea arches and waves crashing under the path.
  • ~1:00 PMDjúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the old lifting stones, with Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (the Journey to the Center of the Earth one) overhead if the cloud lifts.
  • ~3:00 PMKirkjufell + Kirkjufellsfoss for dusk. The arrowhead mountain with the waterfall in front — timed for the end of daylight, which in December means low gold light if it's clear, moody dark if it's not. Either version is the shot.
  • EveningLong dark drive back. This is the latest return of the week — keep the night in town simple: soup in a bread bowl at Svarta Kaffið on Laugavegur is the warm, cheap, TikTok-approved dinner for exactly this situation.
Tired? This is the droppable day. If three tour days in a row sounds like a lot, cut Snæfellsnes and take Thursday as a slow city day (museums, Kolaportið prep, a local pool like Sundhöllin with its rooftop hot tubs) — the trip still works. Keep it if Kirkjufell is a must-see for you; it's the only day that gets you there.
Fri · Dec 18 · Tour day 4 · Last full day

Glacier lagoon + blue ice cave — the winter-only finale

The longest day and the one thing on this trip you literally cannot do in summer: a natural blue ice cave in Vatnajökull, plus icebergs washing up on a black beach. Every TikTok winter route builds toward this day.

Guided tour only — do not self-drive this in DecDepart ~7:00 AM · back ~10–11 PMLagoon at midday light
  • 7:00 AMEarly dark departure. ~380 km each way to Jökulsárlón — most of the drive out is in darkness and twilight, which is why this is a tour-driver day, not a rental-car day. Sleep on the bus; the sights start at midday.
  • ~12:00 PMJökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon in the daylight window. Icebergs calved from the glacier floating to sea, seals if you're lucky, low sun through the ice. This timing is the whole reason for the 7 AM start.
  • ~1:00 PMDiamond Beach, directly across the road: chunks of clear ice on black sand, glowing in the low light. Five minutes from the lagoon, zero extra effort, the most-shared photo of the whole route.
  • AfternoonCrystal ice cave tour (~3 hrs, meets at the lagoon).Winter only Guided, helmets and crampons provided. The blue is real and it only exists roughly November–March — warm spells can move or cancel a cave at short notice, so operators switch caves rather than cancel outright. Book this first, before any other tour.
  • Drive backThe dark return is aurora attempt #5 — lagoon tours watch the sky on the way home and stop if it fires. Back in Reykjavík late: pack tonight, lay out airport clothes, charge everything.
Flex swap — if the ice cave cancels or you want a slower last day: sleep in, do the Blue Lagoon on a late-morning slot (the other lagoon — milky-blue, by the airport road), then a final Reykjavík afternoon: National Museum or the Lava Show, Kolaportið flea market for a wool sweater at non-boutique prices, and a last Bæjarins Beztu hot dog. Move the ice-cave money to a second northern-lights attempt instead.
Sat · Dec 19 · Departure morning

Last morning in Reykjavík

Your flight is 2:05 PM and you leave for the airport about 10:45 AM (Leg 3 below) — so this is a slow, close-to-the-hotel morning, not a sightseeing one.

Leave Reykjavík ~10:45 AMSunrise isn't until ~11:20 AM — it's dark anyway
  • MorningKolaportið flea market (weekends, by the harbour) if you're up early — last chance for a lopapeysa wool sweater — then Brauð & Co for the road, check out, and bags to the Flybus.
  • 10:45 AMLeave for Keflavík — the return timeline picks up right below.
While you're there

Eat this, book this

The short list that comes up in the same TikTok videos over and over — nothing fancy, all walkable from a central Reykjavík hotel.

Brauð & Co — cinnamon roll

The viral one. Go early, eat it warm. Also the grab-and-go breakfast before every 8 AM tour departure.

Bæjarins Beztu — hot dog, með öllu

Iceland's famous stand since 1937. "One with everything" — crispy onion is non-negotiable. Expect a line; it moves fast.

Svarta Kaffið — soup in a bread bowl

Two soups a day (one meat, one veg) on Laugavegur. The default cold-dark-evening dinner in half the winter vlogs.

Café Loki — rye bread ice cream

Opposite Hallgrímskirkja. Geothermal-baked rye bread turned into ice cream — sounds like a gimmick, consistently rated a favourite.

1Ice cave + Jökulsárlón tour (Fri) — book first; small groups, winter-only, sells out and weather-moves.
2Northern Lights tour for Tue night — early booking = free re-runs on Wed/Thu/Fri if it's cloudy or quiet.
3Sky Lagoon, Mon ~5 PM slot — timed entry; dusk slots in December go first.
4Golden Circle (Tue) + South Coast (Wed) tours — or a rental 4×4 with winter tyres if you'd rather drive those two; skip driving Snæfellsnes and the lagoon in December.
5Every morning: road.is + vedur.is before you leave the hotel. Pack waterproof outer layers, warm boots with grip (or cleats), hat and gloves — wind is the real cold in Iceland, not the thermometer.

7:00 PM
Sat, Dec 19

Arrive Zürich Airport ZRH

Iceland and Switzerland are both in Schengen, so there's no passport control on arrival — you walk straight out. On one ticket, checked bags stay with the airline overnight and are reloaded for Tampa; confirm at check-in in Keflavík and keep the claim tag.

18h 45m layover · Zürich (ZRH) — long layover, overnight. Too long to sit in the airport and long enough to actually use. The plan:
~7:30 PMTrain from the airport station to Zürich HB (main station) — about 10–15 min, trains run every few minutes.
EveningCheck in to a hotel near the main station or in the old town. December is Christmas-market season — the market inside the main station hall and the old-town streets along the Limmat are the easy win on a short night.
Sun morningSlow morning in the old town. Be back at the airport by about 11:45 AM — you only need security (bags are already checked), but don't cut it fine.
1:45 PMDepart on WK 4, below.

Arrive Tampa International TPA — home

This is your first US entry point, so passport control, baggage claim, and customs all happen here. Allow ~45–60 min from wheels-down to the curb. Total door-to-door on the way home: 33h 20m, of which 14h 35m is in the air.

Money & bags

  • $867 round trip for 1 passenger in economy — Google Flights flags it low, $474 cheaper than usual for this route.
  • 1st checked bag: $180 on this booking (United out, SWISS/Edelweiss back — bag fees follow each carrier's policy).
  • Budget one Zürich hotel night on top of the fare — the 18h 45m layover isn't in the $867.

The three tight spots

  • Chicago, 1h 5m. Fine if UA 2004 is on time; a delay eats the buffer fast. Sit toward the front if you can.
  • UA 912 and WK 4 both "often delayed 30+ min." Nothing connects after either one, so a delay costs sleep or evening time, not the trip.
  • Zürich bag check-through. It should happen automatically on one ticket — verify when you check in at Keflavík, because if it doesn't, you're collecting and re-checking bags Sunday morning.

Day-plan costs to budget

  • Tours are the big add-on: four guided day tours (Golden Circle, South Coast, Snæfellsnes, glacier lagoon + ice cave) plus a northern-lights tour and Sky Lagoon entry sit on top of the $867 fare and hotels — price them when you book, as December slots and ice-cave places go first.
  • The flex is built in: Snæfellsnes (Thu) is the droppable day, and Friday swaps to Blue Lagoon + city if the ice cave cancels — so a weather day costs a reshuffle, not the trip.
  • Aurora rule: never judge it by one night. The plan gives you up to five attempts (Tue tour + re-runs, Wed/Thu dark drives, Fri lagoon return).
